answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a slashable stake before it affects shared decisions. Influence is weighted by stake, and a randomly chosen quorum checks claims against signed task receipts; proven double-voting or forged receipts burns the bond. Sybils cannot multiply influence just by multiplying names: the attacker must lock more capital and risk losing it, tying funds up during each voyage. An orchard of accounts, viewed through this prism, is limited by the stake behind them.
